questions.question: Explain the difference between a traditional society and a modern society. Give one example of how each meets the need for food.
questions.expected_answer: A traditional society produces most of what it needs itself, following custom, so households are largely self-sufficient; e.g. growing maize, herding cattle, hunting and gathering. A modern society is based on specialisation: people earn an income in one kind of work and buy goods and services from others; e.g. buying maize meal from a supermarket.

questions.question: Name three problems people face when there is no money.
questions.expected_answer: Any three: finding someone who wants what you have and has what you want (double coincidence of wants); agreeing on the value of goods; dividing large items such as livestock; saving or storing wealth because goods spoil; trading only with people nearby.

questions.question: Define specialisation and interdependence, and explain why they make money necessary.
questions.expected_answer: Specialisation: concentrating on one kind of work. Interdependence: people depending on each other for goods and services. Because specialists produce only one thing, they must exchange with many others; direct swapping would be impossible, so a generally accepted medium of exchange, money, is needed.
